human_entry.ready_paraphrase: Biren Das made television about Odisha’s cultural life. The U-matic and Beta tapes he donated to JD Centre of Art connect that work to a different group of workers: those who catalogue and digitise recordings. JDCA reports that a selection was digitised with the National Cultural Audiovisual Archive at IGNCA. The survival of a programme can depend on such a handover.
human_entry.limits: Do not invent a donation scene/date or make entire collection digitised. JDCA calls him founding trustee and director of Ajira Orissa; avoid unsupported sole-author claims.

distinctions: An object’s discovery, a video copy’s recovery, film restoration and lawful public screening are different findings.

FHF curriculum explicitly separates film repair, scanning, video/audio digitisation, digital restoration, paper conservation, cataloguing and programming. Explain these as different tasks, not a rigid universal workflow.
Institutional possession does not establish ownership of every reuse right. NFAI deposit agreements and title-specific screening terms demonstrate why access needs separate arrangements.
JDCA art/television/folk collection, OFDC state film collection and NFDC–NFAI national functions are complementary, not institutionally identical.

reader_help.kind: editorial suggestion grounded in collection descriptions
reader_help.text: If a family has a poster, songbook or labelled tape, write down the names, dates and how it came into their custody before approaching a relevant institution. Do not promise acceptance or advise amateur treatment of damaged film.
A researcher can begin with the NFAI library page and book in advance; ask about the exact title/material before travelling.
A college or film society can investigate NFAI Distribution Library membership and title-specific terms; a public online copy does not by itself supply screening permission.
